subject: history_social
notes: Charles Darwin began developing his theory of evolution by natural selection in the late 1830s, after a five-year voyage aboard HMS Beagle.
For about twenty years, Darwin worked on the theory privately, without publishing it.
In 1858, while collecting specimens in the Malay Archipelago, Alfred Russel Wallace independently arrived at a nearly identical theory and described it in an essay he sent to Darwin.
Later in 1858, papers by both men were presented together at a meeting of the Linnean Society of London.
Darwin published On the Origin of Species in 1859.
stem: The student wants to emphasize that Darwin and Wallace developed the theory independently while acknowledging that their work was first presented jointly. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: After receiving Wallace's 1858 essay describing a nearly identical theory, Darwin published On the Origin of Species in 1859.
choices.B: In 1858, papers by Darwin and Wallace describing evolution by natural selection were presented together at the Linnean Society of London.
choices.C: Though Darwin and Wallace reached the theory of natural selection independently, their papers were first presented together in 1858.
choices.D: While Darwin worked privately on natural selection for about twenty years, Wallace arrived at a nearly identical theory on his own.

explanation.why: The goal has two parts: the two men reached the theory independently, and their work was first presented together. The key must make the independence the main point ("Though … independently") while also acknowledging the joint presentation.
explanation.A: Incorrect. This links Wallace's essay to Darwin's book, but it neither stresses that the discoveries were independent nor mentions the joint presentation.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This reports the joint presentation, but it never says that the two men reached the theory independently.
explanation.C: Correct. It stresses that each man reached the theory independently and acknowledges, in the same sentence, that their papers were presented together.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This shows the independent discoveries clearly, but it leaves out the joint presentation. It is the most attractive near miss.
